final_rationale: The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence. The response mainly narrows and caveats the interpretation of the same record, conceding that the fraud dispute review gap persists, that the affected segment is named in two bank pilot commitments, that legal review is still open, and that there is no completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance. Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance support overall readiness context, but they do not satisfy the internal policy predicate for a material limitation in a named launch use case. Because none of the initial concerns were closed by new admissible evidence, the initial noncompliance finding remains unchanged.
remaining_concerns: The fraud dispute review segment still misses target by 1.3 percentage points.
That segment remains named in two bank pilot commitments, so the weakness remains material under the stated policy.
The product note calling the segment non-core because it is 7% of projected traffic does not resolve materiality for a named committed segment.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open.
The release-policy note still requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The admissible record still contains no completed legal determination, no evidence of completed disclosure, and no approved risk acceptance.
